title: The Ant Highway
text:
If you crouch beside a drain on a hot afternoon, you may find a highway you never noticed. Ants march along it in a thin dark line, each one carrying a crumb, a seed, or a piece of leaf far heavier than itself.
Nobody shouts instructions. Each ant leaves an invisible trail of scent, and the ant behind follows it faithfully. When the food runs out, the scent fades, and the highway quietly disappears.
It is easy to step over them without looking. But a colony of ants can move a whole fallen biscuit across a car park in an afternoon, simply by refusing to give up and by never working alone.
